dhp76:2:
points out
treasure,
the wise one who
seeing your faults
rebukes you.
dhp76:3: Stay with this sort of sage.
dhp76:5:
For the one who stays
with a sage of this sort,
dhp77:2:
deflect you
away from poor manners.
dhp78:1:
Don’t associate with bad friends.
Don’t associate with the low.
dhp79:1:
Drinking the Dhamma,
refreshed by the Dhamma,
one sleeps at ease
dhp79:3:
In the Dhamma revealed
by the noble ones,
the wise person
always delights.
dhp81:1:
As a single slab of rock
won’t budge in the wind,
dhp81:3:
so the wise are not moved
by praise,
by blame.
dhp82:3:
so the wise become clear,
calm,
dhp82:4: on hearing words of the Dhamma.
dhp83:1:
Everywhere, truly,
those of integrity
stand apart.
dhp83:2:
They, the good,
don’t chatter in hopes
of favor or gains.
dhp83:3:
When touched
now by pleasure,
now pain,
dhp83:4:
the wise give no sign
of high
or low.
dhp84:2:
not for his own sake
nor that of another–
dhp84:3:
hanker for
wealth,
a son,
a kingdom,
his own fulfillment,
by unrighteous means:
dhp84:4:
he is
righteous, rich
in virtue,
discernment.
dhp86:1:
But those who practice Dhamma
in line with the well-taught Dhamma,
dhp86:4:
the realm of Death
so hard to transcend.
dhp87:2:
the wise person
should develop the bright,
dhp87:3:
having gone from home
to no-home
dhp87:4: in seclusion, so hard to enjoy.
dhp88:1: There he should wish for delight,
dhp88:2:
discarding sensuality–
he who has nothing.
dhp88:3:
He should cleanse himself–wise–
of what defiles the mind.
dhp89:4:
who delight in non-clinging,
relinquishing grasping–
dhp89:6:
they, in the world,
are Unbound.
